title: Stay safe and make digital payments work for you

say: Stay safe and make digital payments work for you.
This is the video for module 4 of Digital Payments and POS Basics.
You can now pay and get paid in every common way. This module protects what you have built, from tricks and from a stolen phone.

say: Almost every trick creates hurry or confusion, so you hand over your card, PIN, OTP or goods before you check.
For example, Comfort's card does not come out of an ATM in Uyo. A young man tells her to type her PIN again while he holds the slot.

panel.heading: Any hurry is a reason to slow down

say: She recognises the pattern. She steps back, does not re-enter her PIN, and calls the number saved in her phone to block the card.

panel.heading: Any hurry is a reason to slow down

say: She lost a card, which can be replaced, not her savings.

panel.heading: Any hurry is a reason to slow down

say: After a failed payment, fake customer care accounts reply on social media asking for your PIN, OTP or a reversal fee. Real banks never ask for these.

panel.heading: Any hurry is a reason to slow down
panel.rule: PIN, OTP, or a fee to recover your money? It is a scam.

say: Sellers are targeted too. A customer shows a transfer receipt when the queue is long. Check your own history first.

Someone wants to take or update your terminal. Call the provider's official number first.

say: A customer pays, collects, then tells his bank the payment failed. Your APPROVED receipt and record book entry will answer the dispute.

say: And if someone says he is from your terminal provider and must take your terminal, call the provider's official number before handing anything over.

say: For example, Folake's phone is snatched on a bus in Lagos at 6:15 pm. At 6:20 she borrows a colleague's phone and calls her bank on the number written on her card, to block mobile and USSD banking.

say: Next morning she finds no debits. Keep your support numbers on paper too. Lock your phone and apps, and hide OTP previews on the lock screen.

say: Download last month's statement and sort the debits into five or six groups, like food, transport, airtime and data, bills, business stock and charges. Do not count moves between your own accounts.

panel.heading: Your statement is a free record
items: Look for small repeated payments and charges
Pick one change for next month

say: For example, Hadiza, a caterer in Abuja, found 16,000 naira went on small airtime and data top-ups. Any debit you do not recognise? Report it to your bank at once.

say: So she will buy one monthly data plan instead. Pick one change, and read the terms before using any app savings feature.

say: Use direct transfer for customers you know, POS for cards in person, and a payment link for new customers far away.
Paystack's published local fee, checked in October 2026, is 1.5% plus 100 naira, with the 100 waived under 2,500. So Ifeoma's 2,000 naira order costs 30.

say: Plan 30 days with one focus a week. Week 1, setup and safety. Week 2, three payment types. Week 3, business or bills. Week 4, your statement review.
Each week, Rahma spends ten minutes with her app history. Money in was 21,000, then 24,500, then 27,000, then 25,500 naira.
98,000 in, against 68,000 out. Keep your receipts and tables for your certificate, and teach one other woman, by guiding her while she does it herself.

To remember. Hurry is your signal to stop. No one genuine asks for your PIN, OTP or a fee to return your money. If your phone is stolen, block bank, wallet and SIM within the hour. Review your statement monthly, and match the payment method to the customer.
